nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 30 min. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.notes: GET https://api.example.com/v1/assets — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Blend Sources

nodes.name: Roll Up KPIs
nodes.notes: Group-by + aggregate (like a pivot table) — turns raw rows into KPI numbers.

nodes.name: Compose HTML Report
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build an HTML digest table from the aggregated rows Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per asset (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow

Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty price

# Track crypto prices: Google Sheets

**Pattern:** Trading Alert · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers portfolio-tracking work end to end across Google Sheets, Microsoft Teams, Slack and Notion.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Every Few Minutes
2. Gather API Numbers
3. Gather from Google Sheets
4. Blend Sources
5. Roll Up KPIs
6. Compose HTML Report
7. Send Report via Microsoft Teams
8. Load Previous Snapshot
9. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
10. Enrich with Reference Data
11. Fold In Enrichment Fields
12. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
13. Archive Row Snapshot
14. Stamp Completion Time
15. Persist Run Metadata
16. Fingerprint for Idempotency
17. Drop Already-Processed Items
18. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
19. Record Sub-workflow Result
20. Cap Batch Volume
21. Tag Pipeline Metadata
22. Sort Assets Newest First
23. Guard Non-Empty price
24. Save Execution Metadata
25. Stamp Processing Time
26. Align Field Names
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
29. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing portfolio-tracking work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Every Few Minutes → Gather API Numbers → Gather from Google Sheets → Blend Sources → Roll Up KPIs → Compose HTML Report → Send Report via Microsoft Teams → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Cap Batch Volume → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Sort Assets Newest First → Guard Non-Empty price → Save Execution Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Align Field Names → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams aligned by hand for portfolio tracking
- Portfolio tracking work where "Gather API Numbers" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Portfolio tracking work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams in step for portfolio tracking, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Microsoft Teams are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this portfolio-tracking build
- A failed Google Sheets or Microsoft Teams call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this portfolio-tracking build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a portfolio-tracking run reports once rather than 32 times
- Every portfolio-tracking run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

KPIs are rolled up with Summarize (exact group-by + aggregate) before any AI touches the data — asking an LLM to 'figure out the numbers' from raw records is slower, costlier, and less reliable than doing exact arithmetic in n8n and only asking the model to narrate numbers that are already correct.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a second data source and watch it blend into the same report via Merge.
2. Toggle the AI executive-summary step on and off and compare the report's usefulness.
3. Change the KPI grouping field and see how the pivot reshapes.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your portfolio tracking process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole portfolio-tracking payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
